P004-012.context: a resulting outcome; the alternative gloss tác động needs separate contextual review

researchFindings.outcomeVersusImpact: In contemporary lexicography (OALD, CALD, Longman), noun 'effect' spans two primary semantic dimensions: (1) impact/influence on an entity (typically governing 'on/upon') and (2) outcome/result of a cause. In Vietnamese, dimension (1) maps to 'tác động', 'ảnh hưởng', 'hiệu quả', or 'tác dụng', whereas dimension (2) maps to 'kết quả'.
researchFindings.contextsSupportingKetQua: Translating 'effect' as 'kết quả' is attested primarily in logical, philosophical, or fixed phrase patterns: 'cause and effect' (nguyên nhân và kết quả), 'to that effect' (với ý tứ/kết quả đó), 'to little/no effect' (không đem lại kết quả gì).
contextsRequiringAlternativeGlosses: 'have an effect on': 'có tác động / ảnh hưởng đến' (translating as 'có kết quả lên' is unidiomatic/ungrammatical in Vietnamese)
'the effect of heat on metals': 'tác động của nhiệt lên kim loại'
'take effect': 'phát huy tác dụng / có hiệu lực' (never 'lấy kết quả')
'the medicine had no effect': 'thuốc không có tác dụng gì'
researchFindings.senseConstraintAnalysis: The existing English definition ('A change or result caused by an event, action, or other cause.') is polysemous, combining 'change' (impact) and 'result' (outcome). A standalone gloss 'kết quả' covers only the outcome dimension while misrepresenting the predominant verbal complementation pattern with 'on'. The candidate context note explicitly acknowledged this deficit ('the alternative gloss tác động needs separate contextual review').
researchFindings.sourceMappingDefect: The candidate mapping in Pilot 004 included 'source-cambridge-vi-raise' (an irrelevant raise page), and cited 'source-cambridge-vi-effect'. Cambridge English–Vietnamese noun entries provide 'hiệu quả, tác dụng, ấn tượng', but not 'kết quả'.

proposedCASRemediation.proposedContext: impact on someone/something (have an effect on); outcome in cause-and-effect contexts

P004-033.context: causing a quantitative increase, such as transport costs; nâng lên is pending review for other contexts

researchFindings.transitiveQuantitativeIncrease: English 'raise' in this sense is strictly transitive with causative valency [raise + NP] (e.g., raise prices, raise taxes, raise salaries, raise transport costs). The Vietnamese gloss 'làm tăng' precisely encapsulates this causative transitivity ('cause to become greater'), distinguishing it from intransitive 'tăng' (rise).

lexicalComparison.lamTang: Idiomatic and exact for quantitative/financial nouns: 'làm tăng chi phí vận chuyển', 'làm tăng giá cả', 'làm tăng thuế'.
lexicalComparison.nang: Used for abstract qualitative elevation: 'nâng cao tiêu chuẩn' (raise standards), 'nâng cao nhận thức' (raise awareness). Rarely used as standalone 'nâng chi phí'.
lexicalComparison.nangLen: Primarily physical spatial elevation ('nâng cờ lên', 'nâng tạ lên') or figurative ascension; less natural when governing numeric costs directly.

researchFindings.contrastWithRise: English 'rise' is intransitive ('transport costs rose' -> 'chi phí vận chuyển tăng lên'). English 'raise' requires a direct object ('shortage raised transport costs' -> 'sự khan hiếm làm tăng chi phí vận chuyển'). Conflating 'raise' with 'rise' is a frequent learner error that the gloss 'làm tăng' effectively prevents.
researchFindings.sourceMappingDefect: Pilot 004 mapped 'source-cambridge-vi-effect' to this claim in addition to 'source-cambridge-vi-raise'. The effect page is entirely irrelevant and must be removed.

proposedCASRemediation.proposedContext: causing a quantitative increase (prices, costs, taxes); for qualitative targets (standards, awareness) use nâng cao
proposedCASRemediation.sourceMappingCorrection: Remove source-cambridge-vi-effect from mapping; retain source-cambridge-vi-raise

P004-045.context: resource use, such as ink consumption

researchFindings.resourceCarefulUse: English 'economical' specifically denotes avoiding waste in money, fuel, time, or supplies ('an economical car', 'economical with ink'). Vietnamese 'tiết kiệm' is the exact lexicographic equivalent across all major authorities (Cambridge, Oxford, Longman).
researchFindings.economicVersusEconomical: Learners frequently confuse relational adjective 'economic' (thuộc về kinh tế) with evaluative adjective 'economical' (tiết kiệm). Maintaining 'tiết kiệm' as the gloss is pedagogically crucial to prevent false synonymy.

syntacticBehavior.predicative: 'This printer is economical with ink' -> 'Máy in này tiết kiệm mực'

researchFindings.sourceMisattributionRootCause: Pilot 004 mapped candidate gloss-economical-resources to 'source-cambridge-vi-economic' (URL: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english-vietnamese/economic). That URL documents 'economic', NOT 'economical'! Cambridge Dictionary hosts a dedicated entry for 'economical' at https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english-vietnamese/economical which explicitly translates it as 'tiết kiệm' (PASSWORD English–Vietnamese Dictionary, © K Dictionaries Ltd. 2015).

sevenClaimAssessments.canonicalDefinitionEn: Have an influence on or cause a change in someone or something.
sevenClaimAssessments.context: influence on attendance or a comparable outcome

lexicographicAnalysis.semanticRange: Denotes causing an effect or alteration in an entity, condition, or state.
lexicographicAnalysis.contextualEquivalence: Natural Vietnamese rendering in transitive influence contexts: 'ảnh hưởng đến lượng người tham gia'.
lexicographicAnalysis.naturalWording: Vietnamese uses 'ảnh hưởng đến' or 'ảnh hưởng tới' as a verbal phrase taking a prepositional object.
lexicographicAnalysis.registerDifferences: Neutral to formal; suitable across academic and general registers.
lexicographicAnalysis.collocationCompatibility: Compatible with 'lượng người tham gia', 'sức khỏe', 'thời tiết', 'tâm lý'.
lexicographicAnalysis.counterexamples: In emotional shock senses ('deeply affected'), Vietnamese requires 'làm xúc động' or 'làm chạnh lòng'; in pretense senses ('affected indifference'), Vietnamese requires 'giả vờ/ra vẻ'. These are separate omitted senses.
lexicographicAnalysis.falseEquivalenceRisk: Learner confusion with noun 'effect'; gloss correctly anchors verbal influence.
lexicographicAnalysis.crossLingualValency: English transitive verb [affect + NP] corresponds to Vietnamese verb phrase [ảnh hưởng đến + NP].

adversarialReview.q1_impliesDifferentSense: No; 'ảnh hưởng đến' unambiguously targets the influence sense.
adversarialReview.q2_naturalInContext: Yes; 'ảnh hưởng đến lượng người tham gia' is fully natural.
adversarialReview.q3_tooGeneralOrNarrow: Well-calibrated; 'tác động đến' is a near-synonym variant.
adversarialReview.q4_valencyCorresponds: Yes; English direct object corresponds to Vietnamese prepositional complement with 'đến'.
adversarialReview.q6_sourceSupportsExactGloss: Cambridge English–Vietnamese indexed entry gives 'ảnh hưởng, tác động' and attestations with 'đến' (e.g., affects many older people -> ảnh hưởng đến nhiều người cao tuổi).
adversarialReview.q7_inferredFromAIGenerated: No; corroborated by external bilingual dictionary entries.
adversarialReview.q8_contradictoryExample: Only in omitted emotion or pretense senses.
adversarialReview.q9_evidenceIndependentOfAI: Yes; external learner dictionary provides independent grounding.
adversarialReview.q10_remainingUncertainty: Direct page HTTP returned 403; access via search index excerpt. Underlying rights belong to K Dictionaries (reference_only).

sevenClaimAssessments.canonicalDefinitionEn: A change or result caused by an event, action, or other cause.
sevenClaimAssessments.context: a resulting outcome; the alternative gloss tác động needs separate contextual review

lexicographicAnalysis.semanticRange: Dual dimension: impact/influence ('have an effect on') vs outcome/result ('cause and effect').
lexicographicAnalysis.contextualEquivalence: 'kết quả' is valid only in outcome/cause-and-effect contexts; it fails in 'have an effect on' contexts.
lexicographicAnalysis.naturalWording: 'tác động', 'ảnh hưởng', 'hiệu quả' are the standard Vietnamese nouns for 'effect'.
lexicographicAnalysis.collocationCompatibility: 'side effect' -> 'tác dụng phụ'; 'adverse effect' -> 'tác động tiêu cực'; 'cause and effect' -> 'nguyên nhân và kết quả'.
lexicographicAnalysis.counterexamples: 'The radiation had a disastrous effect on health' -> cannot translate as 'kết quả thảm khốc lên sức khỏe'; must be 'tác động/ảnh hưởng thảm khốc'.
lexicographicAnalysis.falseEquivalenceRisk: High risk that learners equate 'effect' with 'result' exclusively and produce unidiomatic Vietnamese phrases.
lexicographicAnalysis.crossLingualValency: English [have an effect on + NP] maps to Vietnamese [có tác động/ảnh hưởng đến + NP].

adversarialReview.q1_impliesDifferentSense: Yes; implies generic outcome (result) rather than impact/effect.
adversarialReview.q2_naturalInContext: Unnatural in verb-governed contexts ('have an effect on').
adversarialReview.q3_tooGeneralOrNarrow: Too narrow in outcome dimension; omits primary impact dimension.
adversarialReview.q5_collocationRisk: High risk: 'kết quả phụ' instead of 'tác dụng phụ'.
adversarialReview.q6_sourceSupportsExactGloss: Contradicted: Cambridge English–Vietnamese gives 'hiệu quả, tác dụng, ấn tượng', not 'kết quả'.
adversarialReview.q7_inferredFromAIGenerated: Yes; original AI candidate adopted school mnemonic without verifying learner entry distribution.
adversarialReview.q8_contradictoryExample: 'The medicine didn't have any effect' -> 'thuốc không có tác dụng gì'.
adversarialReview.q9_evidenceIndependentOfAI: Independent dictionary evidence contradicts 'kết quả' as a standalone headword translation.
adversarialReview.q10_remainingUncertainty: Requires Lead Editorial Reviewer adjudication on whether to split senses or broaden the gloss.

sevenClaimAssessments.canonicalDefinitionEn: Cause a change or outcome to happen.
sevenClaimAssessments.canonicalExampleEn: The revised timetable effected a lasting improvement.
sevenClaimAssessments.context: bringing about a change or improvement

lexicographicAnalysis.semanticRange: Formal causative transitive verb: bring about, achieve, or implement a change/outcome.
lexicographicAnalysis.contextualEquivalence: 'tạo ra' is a loose paraphrase; 'thực hiện' or 'đem lại / mang lại' is the precise formal equivalent.
lexicographicAnalysis.naturalWording: 'thực hiện sự thay đổi' (effect a change), 'đem lại sự cải thiện' (effect an improvement).
lexicographicAnalysis.registerDifferences: English 'effect' (verb) is formal/official/literary; 'tạo ra' is generic/informal.
lexicographicAnalysis.collocationCompatibility: Takes abstract outcome nouns: change, cure, recovery, reform, reconciliation, improvement.
lexicographicAnalysis.counterexamples: 'effect a reconciliation' -> 'đạt được/thực hiện sự hòa giải', not 'tạo ra sự hòa giải'.
lexicographicAnalysis.falseEquivalenceRisk: Learners may assume 'effect' can translate any 'tạo ra' (e.g., *effect a table, *effect a machine - invalid).
lexicographicAnalysis.crossLingualValency: Transitive verb taking an abstract nominal complement.

adversarialReview.q2_naturalInContext: Understandable in 'tạo ra sự cải thiện', but less formal than 'đem lại' or 'thực hiện'.
adversarialReview.q3_tooGeneralOrNarrow: Too general; loses the formal register of 'bring about'.
adversarialReview.q5_collocationRisk: Learner may overgeneralize to physical objects.
adversarialReview.q6_sourceSupportsExactGloss: Cambridge English–Vietnamese lists 'thực hiện', NOT 'tạo ra'.
adversarialReview.q7_inferredFromAIGenerated: Yes; authored example and loose AI gloss.
adversarialReview.q8_contradictoryExample: 'effect a cure' -> 'chữa khỏi / đem lại sự phục hồi'.
adversarialReview.q10_remainingUncertainty: Recommend human editor approve 'thực hiện, đem lại' with formal register tag.

contradictoryEvidenceLedger.contradictoryEvidence: Cambridge English–Vietnamese noun entry for 'effect' lists 'hiệu quả, tác dụng, ấn tượng'. It does NOT list 'kết quả' as a primary nominal translation. Collocations with 'on' ('have an effect on') contradict 'kết quả' because 'có kết quả lên' is unidiomatic Vietnamese.

Cambridge English–Vietnamese verb entry for 'effect' lists 'thực hiện' (effect a change -> thực hiện một sự thay đổi). 'Tạo ra' is generic and fails to represent the formal administrative register of the English verb.

valencyContrastSummary.pedagogicalImplication: Learners frequently omit 'đến' in Vietnamese or incorrectly insert 'to/on' after English 'affect' (*affect to health). Annotating this valency divergence prevents cross-linguistic negative transfer.
Vietnamese 'tăng' can be both transitive and intransitive. Using 'làm tăng' clearly mirrors English 'raise' and prevents confusion with intransitive 'rise'.
